specification.problem: Approximate the single-qubit Markovian semigroup T_t = exp(tL) applied to a density matrix rho, using a second-order product formula over a decomposition of L, with each factor realized as a single-qubit channel via a unitary on system plus one ancilla (ancilla reset to |0> between segments).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: a qubit generator L = L_H + L_deph + L_damp (Hamiltonian rotation, pure dephasing, amplitude damping) with symmetric second-order Trotter with r segments, each segment channel dilated on 1 system + 1 ancilla qubit (2 qubits total). Readout via the system reduced density matrix (statevector, trace out ancilla). Out of scope: the paper's specific decomposition and recombination technique, the specific arbitrary single-qubit channel approximation method and its gate counts, and the proof of the O((||L|| t)^{3/2}/eps^{1/2}) bound.

equations.label: Semigroup
equations.description: Target channel and generator decomposition into simple pieces.
equations.abstract_quote: approximates the channel $T_{t}=e^{t\mathcal{L}}$ up to chosen accuracy $\epsilon$
equations.justification: The channel form is stated; the decomposition into simple terms is inferred from 'decomposition and recombination technique'.
assumptions: The specific decomposition used in the paper is unknown; this one is assumed.

equations.label: Second-order product formula
equations.description: Symmetric Suzuki formula with r segments.
equations.justification: Inspired by Hamiltonian simulation; second-order choice follows the 3/2 exponent but is assumed.
assumptions: Second-order formula used; the paper may use other orders.

equations.label: Trotter error and segment count
equations.description: Error scaling gives segment count consistent with the claimed gate count when each segment costs O(1) gates.
equations.justification: Inverting the standard second-order error gives this r; matches the stated scaling.
assumptions: Norm of terms bounded by a constant times ||L||

equations.label: Dilation of each factor
equations.description: Each single-qubit channel is realized with one ancilla in |0>, then ancilla discarded/reset.
equations.abstract_quote: the algorithm requires only a single ancilla qubit, the minimal possible dilation for a non-unitary single-qubit quantum channel
equations.justification: Single ancilla dilation is stated; Stinespring form with a 2-dim environment is background (Kraus rank <=2 needed here).
assumptions: Each e^{sL_j} in the instance has Kraus rank <=2 (true for dephasing, damping, unitary pieces).

equations.label: Instance channels
equations.latex: K_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\sqrt{1-p}\end{pmatrix},\ K_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&\sqrt p\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\ p=1-e^{-\Gamma s};\quad \text{dephasing: }\rho_{01}\to e^{-\gamma s}\rho_{01};\quad \text{Hamiltonian: }\rho\to e^{-i\omega s Z/2}\rho e^{i\omega sZ/2}
equations.description: Analytic exponentials of the assumed pieces; amplitude damping realized by controlled rotation by angle 2 arcsin sqrt p plus CNOT.
equations.justification: Concrete tiny instance chosen for implementation; standard channels.
assumptions: Pieces commute poorly enough to produce nonzero Trotter error only if the Hamiltonian axis differs, e.g. use H=omega X/2 with damping.

registers.name: anc
registers.role: dilation ancilla, starts and is reset to |0> after each factor

specification.initial_state: sys in a chosen pure state (e.g. |+> or |0>), anc in |0>

steps.description: Choose the instance (rates, t, r) and the decomposition L_1=Hamiltonian, L_2=dephasing, L_3=amplitude damping.
Pick r from the target eps via the error scaling; use second-order symmetric ordering.
For each factor in each segment, apply the dilating unitary on sys+anc with anc in |0>, compiled to standard gates (ry, cx, rz); reset anc to |0>. Unitary pieces need no ancilla.
After r segments, read the reduced density matrix of sys (statevector with ancilla traced out, or Pauli expectation measurements) and compare with exp(tL) rho.

specification.measurement: If counts are required: measure the system in X, Y, Z bases for Bloch vector; otherwise no measurement and use statevector with partial trace. Mid-circuit ancilla reset is assumed allowed.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Reconstruct rho=(I+xX+yY+zZ)/2 from expectations, or take the partial trace; compute exp(tL) via the 4x4 matrix exponential of the Liouvillian and compare in trace distance.
assumptions: Lindblad L with few terms each having analytic exponential
Ancilla reset between segments is allowed
Per-factor channel synthesis is exact or error much smaller than Trotter error
Paper's general channel approximation method replaced by exact dilations for Kraus rank <=2 pieces
